checks.check: cross-process session resume via the Python SDK
checks.detail: JSON-RPC error: session "probe-001" already exists. The pinned SDK server (packages/sdk/server/src/server.ts) exposes only initialize / session/prompt / shutdown and creates a session implicitly via ctx.agents.create(). It has no session/open or session/resume method, so a persisted session id collides on a fresh runtime process. An official resume exists one layer down (AgentFactory.resume) but is not reachable over the SDK wire protocol at this pin.

consequences_for_ravel.master_persistence: A DSH session cannot be reopened across runtime restarts through the pinned SDK. RAVEL therefore treats PostgreSQL Project State plus MasterCheckpoint as the recovery source of truth and rebuilds a replacement Master session under the same Master identity with a fresh session id, as docs/07_DSH_INTEGRATION.md section 8 already prescribes. No recovery path depends on replaying old chat context.
consequences_for_ravel.tool_exposure: The pinned JSON-RPC protocol carries no tool-registration surface in either direction (initialize / session/prompt / shutdown only; server-to-client requests are a dormant capability with no producer). RAVEL tools are therefore exposed to agents as MCP servers over stdio through @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client, which is configuration-only and keeps all tool logic in Python.
consequences_for_ravel.per_session_tool_scope: The SDK server composes sessions without joining an agent preset, so per-session preset selection is unreachable through the pinned SDK. Tool scope is enforced per role by composing one DSH profile per agent role, each mounting only that role's MCP server and prompt sections. This is a documented deviation; see docs/IMPLEMENTATION_DEVIATIONS.md.
consequences_for_ravel.no_core_modification: No DSH core source is modified, forked, or vendored into RAVEL. Only shipped composition mechanisms are used: profiles, profile patch layers, bundles, agent presets, and MCP server rows.
